sealedSource: Structurally modelled on automated welfare debt-recovery programmes that reversed the burden of proof onto low-income claimants.
archetype: HARM UNDER CORRECT OPERATION — the system did exactly what it was designed to do, efficiently, and the harm fell entirely on parties outside the decision.
historicallySupportedMechanisms: An annual-income average was used as if it were an individual measurement of fortnightly entitlement.
The burden of proof was shifted onto claimants with the least practical capacity to contest automated demands.
The system optimised recovery efficiency while exporting error and psychological cost to people outside the decision.
materialisedConsequences: Large numbers of demands issued against people who owed nothing
Severe psychological harm to recipients, including deaths
Recovery ultimately reversed and repaid, at a cost far exceeding the saving
irreversibleThreshold: Trust in the institution — a fragile commons with hysteresis; it did not recover on the timescale it was lost.
absentStakeholder: Claimants, who appear in the evidence only as a category and who had no representation in the decision at all.
narratorContribution: The narrator treated the existence of a dispute channel as equivalent to a usable exit, for a population defined by having the least capacity to use one.
horizonMismatch: Decision horizon six months; legitimacy recovery horizon a decade or more; narrator recorded 'not applicable'.

availableActionsAtDecisionPoint.action: Continue individual/manual verification rather than use annual averaging as the basis for automated debt demands.
Keep the burden on the agency to establish an individual debt before issuing a recovery notice rather than requiring claimants to disprove it.

plausibleUnrealisedRisks: Retaining manual review could be slower and more expensive and could reduce headline recovery efficiency.
irrelevantDistractors: IT delivery failure as the principal mechanism
A data-protection breach as the principal mechanism
nonTargetHistoricalEvents: Staff industrial action occurred but was not the material harm.
